root_cause.text: sch_qfq.c used the shared leaf qdisc queue length (`cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0`) as a proxy for a QFQ class/aggregate being active during `qfq_reset_qdisc()`, even though multiple `qfq_class` instances can reference the same leaf qdisc, causing deactivation of an inactive aggregate and a NULL dereference in `qfq_deactivate_agg`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0)` to `if (cl_is_active(cl))` in `qfq_reset_qdisc()`, and the commit message explicitly states that "`qfq_class->leaf_qdisc->q.qlen > 0` does not imply that the class itself is active" because "Two qfq_class objects may point to the same leaf_qdisc," leading `qfq_reset()` to "wrongly deactivate an inactive aggregate and trigger a null-deref in qfq_deactivate_agg."

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the class active-state check instead of queue length when deactivating classes during QFQ qdisc reset.
intent_record.what: The condition inside qfq_reset_qdisc() was changed from checking `cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0` to calling `cl_is_active(cl)` before invoking `qfq_deactivate_class(q, cl)` while iterating over classes.
intent_record.how: At runtime, class deactivation during qdisc reset is now based on the class's active-state predicate instead of whether its child qdisc queue length is nonzero, which prevents relying on queue length as a proxy for scheduler activity and ensures only actually active classes are deactivated.

Because multiple classes can share the same leaf qdisc, qlen > 0 may be true for an inactive class, leading to incorrect deactivation and eventual NULL dereference in qfq_deactivate_agg.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full `qfq_reset_qdisc()` implementation and the related activation/deactivation logic. The vulnerable construct is present in `qfq_reset_qdisc()`: `hlist_for_each_entry(cl, n, &q->clhash.hash[i], common.hnode) { if (cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0) qfq_deactivate_class(q, cl); qdisc_reset(cl->qdisc); }`. This uses the shared leaf qdisc queue length `cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0` as the condition for whether a class should be deactivated. From the same commit, classes can share a leaf qdisc through aggregates (`struct qfq_class` has `struct qfq_aggregate *agg;`, and activity is tracked per-aggregate via `struct list_head active`). `qfq_deactivate_class()` does `list_del(&cl->alist);` and only then checks `if (list_empty(&agg->active)) qfq_deactivate_agg(q, agg);`, which assumes the class is actually on the aggregate active list. Therefore, if multiple `qfq_class` instances reference the same leaf qdisc, `cl->qdisc->q.qlen > 0` may be true for an inactive class, causing `qfq_deactivate_class()` to run on a class not active in QFQ bookkeeping, matching the described root cause. There is no fix present here such as checking real class/aggregate activity state before deactivation; the code still relies on qlen as a proxy. Hence `has_bug=true` and `is_fixed=false`.
